extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers seeking an encyclopedic biography of Sabrina Erdely and accounts of the Rolling Stone controversy (also useful to journalists and media-ethics observers)
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing Sabrina Rubin Erdely's life, career, high-profile Rolling Stone article 'A Rape on Campus', the subsequent retraction, editorial reviews, and related legal actions and criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic, even routine journalistic practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Columbia University School of Journalism review concluded that Erdely and Rolling Stone failed to engage in "basic, even routine journalistic practice."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied components (from surrounding article text): verify and corroborate accounts, seek independent confirmation, obtain corroborating documents and official records, check consistency of source accounts, and follow standard fact-checking procedures. The Columbia review motivated Rolling Stone's retraction and widespread criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual malice (defamation standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: A federal jury found Erdely liable for defamation with "actual malice" — concluding she knew statements about Nicole Eramo were false—or had reason to doubt them and failed to investigate further—but published them anyway.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal standard used in the case: publisher/author must not publish knowing falsehoods or with reckless disregard for truth. In practice this requires demonstrable investigation and good-faith efforts to verify contested or potentially defamatory factual claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source reliability and avoiding over-reliance on dubious sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Erdely's reporting was criticized for over-reliance on a dubious source (e.g., the 'Billy Doe' case) and failing to include background material that could have impugned the source's credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance from criticisms/examples in the article: assess source credibility (criminal history, consistency of accounts), corroborate sensitive claims with additional independent sources, and do not center a major narrative on a lone unverified or unreliable source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid confirmation bias / do not 'look for facts to fit a theory'
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics charged Erdely 'did not construct a story based on facts, but went looking for facts to fit her theory.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic best practice implied: approach reporting without a preconceived narrative, consider alternative explanations, actively seek disconfirming evidence, and avoid selecting or shaping facts solely to support a prior hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and management of conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes Erdely's husband was a criminal prosecutor for the District Attorney of Philadelphia while she covered related stories; Rolling Stone editors said this was not a conflict because he was not personally involved in the prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: disclose potential conflicts of interest and evaluate whether they could reasonably affect reporting; editors should assess and make transparent any relationships that might create real or perceived bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight and accountability (audit of editorial processes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rolling Stone's publisher asked the dean of the Columbia Journalism School to audit the editorial processes that led to publication of the controversial story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied editorial standards: robust editorial review, fact-checking workflows, verification checkpoints for high-risk long-form pieces, and willingness to correct/retract when serious errors are found. The Columbia audit and Rolling Stone's apologies/retraction are presented as consequences of failures in these processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirement in defamation ('of and concerning')
rubrics_metrics.description: The Second Circuit found plaintiffs plausibly alleged that purportedly defamatory statements in the article were 'of and concerning' them individually, including under a theory of small group defamation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal criterion for defamation: whether allegedly defamatory statements reasonably identify the plaintiff(s). For small-group defamation, statements that implicitly or explicitly point to identifiable individuals can meet this requirement even if names are not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration with official records and law-enforcement findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Charlottesville police investigation 'found no basis to conclude that anything happened' at the fraternity and found no evidence to support the account alleged in the Rolling Stone article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied practice: cross-check source claims against police reports, investigative records, medical records, and other official documentation when available; treat absence of corroboration as a significant factor in evaluating extraordinary allegations.
